nodes.title: Neatness does not depend on the representation
nodes.statement: If ρ(g) is neat for one faithful representation ρ of G then σ(g) is neat for every representation σ of G defined over a subfield of ℂ.
hypotheses: G a finite-type linear algebraic group over the number field F

ρ is a faithful algebraic representation (a closed immersion), σ is an algebraic representation, and the compared complex point actions use the same embedding F→ℂ. Arbitrary homomorphisms of the abstract rational-point group are excluded.
proofSteps: Every representation σ is a subquotient of a direct sum of tensor products of ρ, ρ^∨ (faithfulness, Chevalley).
Eigenvalues of σ(g) are products of eigenvalues of ρ(g) and their inverses, hence lie in the group generated by the eigenvalues of ρ(g).
acceptance: For GL_n the determinant of a neat element is neat.

sources.match: Exactly the argument.

nodes.title: Neatness is stable under subgroups, conjugation and homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Subgroups of neat subgroups are neat; conjugates of neat subgroups by elements of G(F) are neat; and for a homomorphism φ : G → G′ of linear algebraic groups the image φ(Γ) of a neat subgroup Γ is neat.
hypotheses: G, G′ linear algebraic over F
proofSteps: Subgroups: by definition.
Conjugation preserves eigenvalues.
Homomorphisms: σ ∘ φ is a representation of G; apply neat-representation-independence.
acceptance: The image of a neat subgroup of SL_2(ℚ) in PGL_2(ℚ) is neat.

sources.match: Neat subgroups; stability follows from the representation independence.

nodes.title: Neat groups are torsion free
nodes.statement: A neat subgroup of G(F) is torsion free.
proofSteps: The eigenvalues of an element of finite order are roots of unity, so they generate a finite subgroup, which must be trivial; a diagonalizable (finite-order) element with all eigenvalues 1 is the identity.
acceptance: Γ(N) ⊂ SL_2(ℤ) is torsion free for N ≥ 3.

sources.match: The key observation.

nodes.title: A one-prime criterion for neatness
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G ↪ GL_n be a faithful representation over ℚ (after restriction of scalars) and U ⊂ G(𝔸_f) compact open. If for some prime p ≥ 3 the projection of ρ(U) to GL_n(ℚ_p) lies in 1 + p M_n(ℤ_p) (for p = 2, in 1 + 4M_n(ℤ_2)), then U is neat.
proofSteps: For γ ∈ G(ℚ) ∩ xUx⁻¹, ρ(γ) is conjugate in GL_n(ℚ_p) to an element of x_p ρ(U_p) x_p⁻¹, whose eigenvalues λ in ℚ̄_p satisfy |λ − 1|_p ≤ p⁻¹ (resp. 4⁻¹) because they are eigenvalues of conjugates of elements of 1 + pM_n(ℤ_p).
The multiplicative group {λ : |λ − 1|_p < p^{-1/(p−1)}} of ℚ̄_p contains no nontrivial root of unity, and it contains the group generated by such eigenvalues.
Embedding the eigenvalue group (inside ℚ̄^×) in both ℂ^× and ℚ̄_p^× gives the same abstract group, so it is torsion free.
acceptance: U(3) ⊂ GL_2(ℤ̂) is neat; U(2) is not (it contains −1).

sources.match: Neat congruence subgroups; the p-adic eigenvalue criterion is the standard proof (Borel 17.4, not read).

nodes.title: Neat levels exist
nodes.statement: Every compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) contains a neat normal open subgroup of finite index; every arithmetic subgroup of G(F) contains a neat subgroup of finite index defined by congruence conditions (Borel).
proofSteps: Choose p≥3 and a ρ(U_p)-stable ℤ_p-lattice (compactness gives one); express ρ in that basis. Intersect U with the kernel of reduction on that lattice. This is normal, open and finite index, and neat by neat-criterion-one-prime. Alternatively take the finite normal core in U of an open neat intersection; neatness is preserved under subgroups.
For an arithmetic Γ, intersect with the corresponding congruence subgroup.
acceptance: GL_2(ℤ̂) ⊃ U(3) neat of index #GL_2(ℤ/3) = 48.

sources.match: Exactly the arithmetic-subgroup statement; the adelic level statement is derived here (RT-AREA-automorphic-1/28).

nodes.title: Nested-level map on double cosets
nodes.statement: For a group G, H ≤ G and K′ ≤ K ≤ G, π : H\G/K′ → H\G/K, [g] ↦ [g], is well defined and surjective, and for each g the map K/K′ → π⁻¹([g]), kK′ ↦ [gk], is a surjection; no normality is assumed.
proofSteps: Well defined by DoubleCoset.eq.
Surjectivity onto the fibre: an element of the fibre is [x] with x = h g k, and [x] = [g k] at the finer level.
acceptance: K′ = K gives the identity with singleton fibres.
H = 1: fibres are exactly K/K′.

nodes.title: Level quotients
nodes.statement: For compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) and a closed subgroup K_∞ ⊂ G(F_∞) (for example a maximal compact subgroup times A_G(ℝ)^0, or trivial), the level quotient is X_U = G(F)\G(𝔸_F)/K_∞U with the quotient topology, together with the right action of G(𝔸_f) by Hecke translation X_{gUg⁻¹} ≃ X_U, [x] ↦ [xg].
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Quotient of G(𝔸) by the left action of G(F) and right action of K_∞U.
Right translation by g carries the K_∞(gUg⁻¹)-orbits to K_∞U-orbits.
acceptance: For K_∞ = 1, X_U ≃ ⊔ Γ_i\G(F_∞) (AA.3/component-decomposition).

For GL_2/ℚ and principal K(N), K∞=ℝ^×SO(2) gives φ(N) copies of Γ(N)\ℍ. With K∞=ℝ^×O(2), the negative-determinant involution identifies the pair of half-plane components, giving determinant classes (ℤ/N)^×/{±1}, hence φ(N)/2 components for N≥3.

nodes.title: Covering maps between neat levels
nodes.statement: Let U′⊂U be compact open with U neat, and K∞ containing A_G(ℝ)^0 and compact modulo it. Then X_{U′}→X_U is a finite covering of degree [U:U′]. If U′ is normal in U, the canonical U/U′ action is free and transitive on each fibre, so this is a principal U/U′ covering. The rational stabilizer is trivial in this scope. Equality of U/U′ with the full deck-transformation group additionally requires the usual connectedness hypotheses (in particular connected total space).
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
K∞ contains A_G(ℝ)^0 and is compact modulo it
proofSteps: The fibre over [g] is the orbit set of the finite stabilizer group G(F) ∩ g K_∞U g⁻¹ acting on the cosets of U′ in U (double-coset-level-map with H the stabilizer).
Under the compact-modulo-A_G hypotheses the full rational stabilizer is finite; neatness makes it torsion free and therefore trivial.

For normal U′ the finite U/U′ action is free and properly discontinuous. Identify its orbit quotient with X_U with the actual quotient topology and apply the pinned quotient-covering theorem; use the Tau Ceti intermediate-cover result for nonnormal U′.
acceptance: For GL_2/ℚ with K_∞ = ℝ^×O(2), U = U(3) and U′ = U(9), the covering has degree [U(3) : U(9)] = 3⁴ = 81; the central correction is trivial because −1 ∉ U(3).
Without neatness the map SL_2(ℤ)\ℍ ← Γ(2)\ℍ is not a covering map: it ramifies over the elliptic points i and ρ.

nodes.title: Fibre mass of a level map with stabilizers
nodes.statement: Without neatness, for U′ ⊂ U and x ∈ X_U with finite stabilizer group Γ_x = (G(F) ∩ g K_∞U g⁻¹)/(Z(F) ∩ K_∞U), the fibre of X_{U′} → X_U over x satisfies ∑_{y ↦ x} 1/|Γ_y| = [U : U′]/(|Γ_x|·[Z(F) ∩ K_∞U : Z(F) ∩ K_∞U′]).
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: The fibre is Γ_x\(U/U′) up to the central correction; orbit–stabilizer gives ∑ over orbits of |Γ_x|/|Γ_y| = [U : U′] after removing the central kernel.
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ)\ℍ ← Γ_0(2)\ℍ over the elliptic point i (stabilizer of order 2 mod ±1) the masses add to 3/2 = 3/|Γ_i|.

nodes.title: Quotient groupoids at non-neat level
nodes.statement: For compact open U and closed K∞, 𝒳_U is the action groupoid of G(F) on G(𝔸)/K∞U, with automorphism group G(F)∩xK∞Ux⁻¹ and isomorphism classes X_U. If K∞ contains A_G(ℝ)^0 and is compact modulo it, these automorphism groups are finite; at neat U they are trivial. For an arbitrary closed K∞ they need not be finite (real quadratic unit stabilizers when K∞ is the full archimedean centre).
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Use CategoryTheory.ActionCategory and compute stabilizers directly.

Under the additional compact-modulo-A_G hypothesis, every rational stabilizer element has H_G=0; its finite part lies in a compact subgroup, hence all finite character absolute values are 1. The archimedean stabilizer is therefore in K∞∩ker H_G, which is compact. Discreteness of rational points then makes the full stabilizer finite. This compactness lemma is a recorded gap.
At neat level the actual stabilizer is finite and torsion free, so it is trivial, not merely central.
acceptance: For SL_2/ℚ and U = SL_2(ℤ̂), the automorphism group of the object over i is ⟨S⟩ of order 4.

nodes.title: Cartesian squares of level maps
nodes.statement: Let U′,L⊂U be compact open with U neat, K∞ containing A_G(ℝ)^0 and compact modulo it, and U′L=U. Then X_{U′∩L}→X_L, X_{U′∩L}→X_{U′}, X_{U′}→X_U, X_L→X_U is Cartesian. For L=U_g this identifies this one leg of a Hecke pullback only when the product condition holds. U′ normal does not imply that condition, and U′∩U_g is generally different from U′∩gU′g⁻¹.
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
K∞ contains A_G(ℝ)^0 and is compact modulo it
proofSteps: At neat level all maps are coverings with fibres U/U′, L/(U′ ∩ L) (level-covering-map).
The fibre-product's fibre over a point of X_L is U/U′; the natural map from L/(U′ ∩ L) is bijective iff U′L = U.
A bijective map of coverings over X_L is a homeomorphism.
acceptance: If U′L ≠ U the square is not Cartesian: degrees differ.

nodes.title: Volume of a level quotient
nodes.statement: With a Haar measure dg_f on G(𝔸_f), dg_∞ on G(F_∞) and the product measure on G(𝔸) (AA.0/restricted-haar-split), vol(G(F)\G(𝔸)^1) = vol(U) ∑_{i} vol(Γ_i\G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0) for representatives x_i of G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/U, where Γ_i = G(F) ∩ x_iUx_i⁻¹, the measure on G(𝔸)^1 is transported from G(𝔸)/A_G(ℝ)^0 (AA.2/split-centre-decomposition) and G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0 carries the quotient measure. (G(𝔸)^1 is not G(F_∞)^1 × G(𝔸_f): finite ideles have nontrivial norms.)
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: G(F)\G(𝔸)^1 ≅ G(F)\G(𝔸)/A_G(ℝ)^0 (AA.2/quotient-norm-one-comparison).
AA.3/component-decomposition: G(F)\G(𝔸)/A_G(ℝ)^0 U is the disjoint union of the Γ_i\G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0, and the fibre over each point is a translate of U.
Quotient-measure transitivity gives the product of vol(U) and the archimedean volumes.
acceptance: For SL_2/ℚ: vol(SL_2(ℚ)\SL_2(𝔸)) = vol(SL_2(ℤ̂)) vol(SL_2(ℤ)\SL_2(ℝ)).
For GL_1/ℚ with the idele measure and U = ℤ̂^×: vol(ℚ^×\𝔸^1) = 1 · vol({±1}\ℝ^×/ℝ_{>0}) = 1.

nodes.title: Volumes under finite-index level change
nodes.statement: For compact open U′ ⊂ U, ∑_j vol(Γ′_j\G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0) = [U : U′] ∑_i vol(Γ_i\G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0).
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Both sides times vol(U′), resp. vol(U), equal vol(G(F)\G(𝔸)^1) (quotient-volume-decomposition); vol(U) = [U : U′] vol(U′) (MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure).

nodes.title: The subgroup G(𝔸)^+ from the simply connected cover
nodes.statement: For G connected reductive over F with simply connected cover ρ : G̃ → G^der ⊂ G of the derived group, G(𝔸_F)^+ = ρ(G̃(𝔸_F)), a normal subgroup of G(𝔸_F) containing the commutator subgroup; likewise G(R)^+ for any F-algebra R. For G = PB^× (B a quaternion algebra over ℚ), G̃ = B^(1) is the norm-one group.
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Image of a homomorphism (AA.1/adelic-map).
Normal because G acts on G̃ by conjugation lifting conjugation on G^der.
Contains commutators because the commutator map G × G → G^der lifts to G̃ (Deligne).
acceptance: For G = GL_n, G(𝔸)^+ = SL_n(𝔸).
For G = PGL_2, G(𝔸)^+ is the image of SL_2(𝔸), and G(𝔸)/G(𝔸)^+ ≃ 𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} via det.

nodes.title: The residual quotient G_res
nodes.statement: G_res = G(F)\G(𝔸_F)/G(𝔸_F)^+ = G(𝔸_F)/G(F)G(𝔸_F)^+, an abelian topological group, with π^+ : [G(𝔸)] → G_res the quotient map; the composite G(𝔸) → [G(𝔸)] → G_res is a continuous surjective homomorphism. For G = PB^× over ℚ, G_res is a compact abelian group.
hypotheses: G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: G(F)G(𝔸)^+ is a normal subgroup (plus-subgroup normal) containing commutators, so the quotient is an abelian group.
Compactness for G = PB^×: G_res ≃ ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} (reduced-norm-components), which is compact (GlobalNumberFields layer 6: compact norm-one idele class group, with ℝ_{>0} ⊂ 𝔸^{×2}).

nodes.title: Reduced norms of a quaternion algebra over ℚ
nodes.statement: For a quaternion algebra B over ℚ: Nrd(B_p^×) = ℚ_p^× for every prime p; Nrd(B_∞^×) = ℝ^× if B is split at ∞ and ℝ_{>0} otherwise; and Nrd(B^×) = ℚ^× if B is split at ∞, ℚ_{>0} otherwise (Hasse–Schilling–Maass).
hypotheses: B a quaternion algebra over ℚ
proofSteps: Locally the split case uses determinant. In the division case the unramified quadratic subfield supplies every unit norm and norms of even valuation; a uniformizer of the quaternion division algebra has reduced norm of valuation 1, supplying odd valuation. Equivalently use the Kneser local torsor theorem with its recorded gap.

Global: x is a reduced norm iff the quinary form Nrd ⊥ ⟨−x⟩ has an isotropic vector with nonzero last coordinate; for x > 0 (or B split at ∞) it is indefinite, hence isotropic by Hasse–Minkowski (GlobalQuadraticForms layer 5), and if the isotropic vector has last coordinate 0 then B is split and det represents x anyway.
acceptance: For B = (−1, −1)_ℚ (Hamilton), every positive rational is a sum of four squares.

sources.match: Exactly the global statement.

nodes.title: The reduced norm on the residual quotient
nodes.statement: For G = PB^× with B a quaternion algebra over ℚ, the reduced norm induces an injective continuous homomorphism of locally compact groups Nrd : G(𝔸)/G(𝔸)^+ → 𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2}, and a bijection (indeed an isomorphism of compact groups) G_res ≃ ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} whether or not B is split at ∞. Neither G(𝔸)/G(𝔸)^+ nor 𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} is compact.
hypotheses: B a quaternion algebra over ℚ
proofSteps: Kernel of Nrd on G(ℚ_v) modulo squares is the image of B^(1)(ℚ_v) (local surjectivity, quaternion-reduced-norm-image); hence injectivity.
Image: all of 𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} if B is split at ∞, and (ℝ_{>0} × 𝔸_f^×)/𝔸^{×2} otherwise.

Modulo rational points: Nrd(B^×) = ℚ^× or ℚ_{>0}; in the definite case ℚ_{>0}\(ℝ_{>0} × 𝔸_f^×)/𝔸^{×2} → ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} is bijective because −1 ∈ ℚ^× moves the sign at ∞ (correcting Khayutin's 'index-2 image', E39).
acceptance: For B = M_2(ℚ), G_res ≃ ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} via det.

sources.match: As printed ('compact', and image of index 2 in the definite case); corrected per Khayutin E39/E40 recorded in the reviewed extraction.

nodes.title: Images of tori in the residual quotient
nodes.statement: For a quadratic field E ⊂ B and the torus T = E^×/ℚ^× ⊂ G = PB^×, π^+([T(𝔸)]) is a closed subgroup of G_res and Nrd ∘ π^+([T(𝔸)]) = ker χ_E, where χ_E : ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} → {±1} is the quadratic character of E/ℚ.
proofSteps: T is ℚ-anisotropic, so [T(𝔸)] is a compact abelian group and its image is closed (Khayutin E10 corrects 'isotropic').
Nrd restricted to E^× is the field norm N_{E/ℚ}; its image modulo ℚ^×𝔸^{×2} is ℚ^× N(𝔸_E^×)/…, which is ker χ_E by class field theory (ClassFieldTheory layers 11–12).
acceptance: For E = ℚ(i) ⊂ (−1,−1)_ℚ, the image is the kernel of the character of ℚ(i)/ℚ.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.6, arXiv v3 p. 25; Annals pp. 172–173
sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Limit behaviour of the residual spectrum
nodes.statement: Let B be a quaternion algebra over ℚ, G = PB^×, and for each i let T_i = E_i^×/ℚ^× ⊂ G be the torus of a quadratic field E_i ⊂ B, g_i, s_i ∈ G(𝔸), and μ_i the pushforward to [G(𝔸)] × [G(𝔸)] of the Haar probability measure of [T_i(𝔸)] under t ↦ ([t g_i], [t s_i g_i]). Suppose either the E_i are pairwise distinct (put H = G_res) or all equal one field E_0 (put H = ker(χ_{E_0} ∘ Nrd) < G_res). Then every weak-* limit point of (π^+ × π^+)_* μ_i is an H^Δ-invariant probability measure supported on a single coset of H^Δ; in general (π^+ × π^+)_* μ_i need not converge.
proofSteps: (π^+ × π^+)_* μ_i is the Haar probability measure on the coset of the closed subgroup π^+([T_i(𝔸)])^Δ through (π^+(g_i), π^+(s_ig_i)) (torus-image-residual).

Distinct fields give distinct characters χ_i; since the Pontryagin dual of the compact group ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2} is discrete, the subgroups ker χ_i converge in the Chabauty topology to the whole group, so limits are invariant under H^Δ = G_res^Δ.
Equal fields: the invariance group is constant, H^Δ.
Non-convergence: the cosets need not converge, only along subsequences (Remark 3.7).
acceptance: For E_i = E_0 fixed, limits are supported on a coset of ker(χ_{E_0} ∘ Nrd)^Δ.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.6, arXiv v3 p. 24; Annals p. 172
sources.match: Exactly the conclusion.

sources.locator: Remark 3.7, arXiv v3 p. 25; Annals p. 172
sources.match: The non-convergence.

nodes.title: The GL_1 quotient is the idele class group
nodes.statement: For G = G_m over a number field F: G(F)\G(𝔸_F) ≃ₜ* IdeleClassGroup F; G(𝔸_F)^1 is the group 𝔸_F^1 of norm-one ideles; A_G(ℝ)^0 = ℝ_{>0} embedded diagonally at the archimedean places; 𝔸_F^× = 𝔸_F^1 × ℝ_{>0}; and F^×\𝔸_F^1 is compact while F^×\𝔸_F^× is not.
proofSteps: AA.1/gm-adelic identifies the groups; the quotient topologies agree.
X*_F(G_m) = ℤ·id, so H_G = log ‖·‖ and G(𝔸)^1 = 𝔸^1 (AA.2/norm-one-subgroup).
A_G = G_m ⊂ Res_{F/ℚ} G_m, so A_G(ℝ)^0 = ℝ_{>0}; split-centre-decomposition.
Compactness: GlobalNumberFields layer 6 (or AA.3/compactness-anisotropic, G_m^der = 1).
acceptance: For F = ℚ: ℚ^×\𝔸^1 ≃ ℤ̂^×, of ideleHaar volume 1.

sources.match: The GL_1 case n = 1.
Exactly the compactness check.

nodes.title: GL_1 class number
nodes.statement: For G = G_m over F and U = Ô^× = ∏_v 𝒪_v^×, G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/U ≃ Cl(𝒪_F), so its cardinality is the class number of F.
proofSteps: The map from finite ideles to fractional ideals, x ↦ ∏ 𝔭_v^{v(x_v)}, is surjective with kernel Ô^× and sends F^× to principal ideals (Borel 2.2; GlobalNumberFields layer 4 finite-idele description of the class group).
Compare with AA.3/class-number-finite.
acceptance: For F = ℚ(√−5) the double coset space has 2 elements.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Geometry of the GL_1 arithmetic quotients X_Q
nodes.statement: For a finite set Q of finite places with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^n, let U_Q = K_∞ × ∏_v U_{Q,v}, where K_∞ ≅ (S¹)^{r₂} is the identity component of the maximal compact subgroup of (F ⊗ ℝ)^×, U_{Q,v} = 𝒪_v^× for v ∉ Q and the index-p^n subgroup of 𝒪_v^× for v ∈ Q, and X_Q = F^×\𝔸_F^×/U_Q A_∞^0 with A_∞^0 = A_{G_m}(ℝ)^0. Each connected component of X_Q is a compact torus (S¹)^{r₁+r₂−1}, and π_0(X_Q) = F^×\𝔸_F^×/U_Q (F ⊗ ℝ)^{×,0}, an extension of the narrow class group of F by a quotient of ∏_{v∈Q} 𝒪_v^×/𝒪_v^{×p^n} (not, in general, the maximal exponent-p^n quotient of the ray class group).
proofSteps: AA.3/component-decomposition for G_m with level U_Q: components are Γ\(F ⊗ ℝ)^×/ℝ_{>0} with Γ = F^× ∩ U_Q a finite-index subgroup of the units.

After dividing by K∞=(S¹)^{r₂}, the archimedean identity component modulo A∞^0 is ℝ^{r₁+r₂−1} in logarithmic coordinates. The positive congruence-unit subgroup is a full lattice of that rank (gl1-units-lattice). Each component is therefore a torus of dimension r₁+r₂−1; the complex circles were already divided out.
π_0 is the quotient by the identity component (F ⊗ ℝ)^{×,0} (correcting Calegari–Geraghty's description, E160 of the reviewed extraction).
acceptance: For F = ℚ, X_Q is finite (r₁ + r₂ − 1 = 0) and π_0(X_Q) = ℚ^×\𝔸^×/U_Q ℝ_{>0} ≅ ℤ̂^×/U_Q.
For F real quadratic and Q = ∅, X_Q has h⁺_F components, each a circle.

sources.match: The components; the component group is corrected (E160 of the reviewed extraction).

nodes.title: The invariant l0 for GL_1
nodes.statement: Every connected component of X_Q has dimension r₁ + r₂ − 1 = NumberField.Units.rank F, the value of Calegari–Geraghty's invariant l0 for G = GL_1/F; in particular its cohomology vanishes above degree r₁ + r₂ − 1.
proofSteps: Dimension of the torus of gl1-XQ-components; r₁ + r₂ = #InfinitePlace F (Mathlib), so the dimension is Units.rank F.
acceptance: For F imaginary quadratic, l0 = 0.

sources.match: Exactly the value.

nodes.title: Degree-zero cohomology of X_Q
nodes.statement: The ℤ_p-module of locally constant functions X_Q → ℤ_p is free on π_0(X_Q): H^0(X_Q, ℤ_p) ≅ ℤ_p[π_0(X_Q)].
proofSteps: X_Q is a finite disjoint union of its connected components (finitely many, by AA.3/class-number-finite), each connected; locally constant functions are constant on components.
acceptance: For F = ℚ and Q = ∅, H^0(X, ℤ_p) = ℤ_p (one component).

sources.match: H^0 is the group ring of the component group (here with the corrected component group).

nodes.title: Hecke and diamond operators for GL_1
nodes.statement: For v ∉ Q with uniformizer π_v, the Hecke correspondence T_{π_v} (AA.4/hecke-correspondence for g = π_v at v) is right translation by π_v, acting on π_0(X_Q) by multiplication by the class [π_v]; for v ∈ Q and α ∈ 𝒪_v^×, the diamond operator ⟨α⟩ is right translation by α. Since all operators are translations they act compatibly on H^0 and, through the Künneth decomposition of each torus component, identically on all cohomological degrees.
proofSteps: G_m is abelian, so U_Q π_v U_Q = π_v U_Q and the Hecke correspondence is a single translation.
Translation permutes the components by the class of π_v in π_0 and maps each torus component to another by a translation, which acts trivially on the cohomology of the torus up to that permutation.
acceptance: For F = ℚ and Q = ∅, T_p acts on π_0 = point trivially.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: The GL_2/ℚ quotient and the upper half-plane
nodes.statement: For G = GL_2 over ℚ, K_∞ = ℝ^× SO(2) and U ⊂ GL_2(𝔸_f) compact open, G(ℚ)\G(𝔸)/K_∞U ≃ ⊔_{c ∈ ℚ_{>0}\𝔸_f^×/det U} Γ_c\ℍ, where Γ_c = GL_2(ℚ)^+ ∩ g_c U g_c⁻¹ for g_c ∈ GL_2(𝔸_f) with det g_c = c, acting on ℍ by Möbius transformations; for det U = ℤ̂^× there is a single component.
proofSteps: Use gl2-real-quotient and upper-half-plane-action-conventions: the raw GL₂(ℝ) action gives ℍ±, whereas Mathlib glAction is its folded ℍ version. The rational negative-determinant matrix exchanges the two half-planes, so one may restrict to ℍ and GL₂(ℚ)^+.
π_0 = GL_2(ℚ)^+\GL_2(𝔸_f)/U ≃ ℚ_{>0}\𝔸_f^×/det U by class-set-abelianization (SL_2 is simply connected with SL_2(ℝ) noncompact; strong approximation for SL_2).
AA.3/component-decomposition then identifies each component; the analytic identification of Γ\ℍ with the modular curve is ModularCurvesPartII R12.2.
acceptance: For U = GL_2(ℤ̂): SL_2(ℤ)\ℍ (one component).
For U = K(N): (ℤ/N)^× copies of Γ(N)\ℍ (gl2-principal-level).

sources.match: Exactly the decomposition for (GL_2, ℍ^±).

uses.how: the classical/adelic function dictionary for GL_2 (RS-04 link AA.5 → AF.5)
underlying GL_2 quotient comparison (RS-04 link AA.5 → V8)

nodes.title: Principal congruence level
nodes.statement: For U = K(N) = ker(GL_2(ℤ̂) → GL_2(ℤ/N)), det K(N) = {x ∈ ℤ̂^× : x ≡ 1 mod N}, the components are indexed by (ℤ/N)^×, and each Γ_c is Γ(N) = ker(SL_2(ℤ) → SL_2(ℤ/N)) (Mathlib CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma).
proofSteps: GL_2(ℚ)^+ ∩ K(N) = SL_2(ℤ) ∩ K(N) = Γ(N) (determinant a positive unit of ℤ is 1); other components are conjugate by elements of GL_2(ℤ̂) normalizing K(N) with determinant c.
acceptance: For N = 1 or 2 there is one component.

sources.match: The groups Γ_c.

nodes.title: Compactness for a definite quaternion algebra
nodes.statement: For a definite quaternion algebra D over ℚ and G = D^×: G(ℚ)\G(𝔸)^1 is compact; G(ℚ)\G(𝔸_f)/U is finite for every compact open U; each Γ_{x,U} = D^× ∩ xUx⁻¹ is finite; and D^×/ℚ^× is discrete in (D ⊗ 𝔸_f)^×/𝔸_f^×.
hypotheses: D a quaternion division algebra over ℚ with D ⊗ ℝ ≅ ℍ (Hamilton)
proofSteps: G^der = SL_1(D) is anisotropic: D is a division algebra, so D^× has no nontrivial unipotent elements (a unipotent u gives the nilpotent u − 1 ≠ 0 in D); apply AA.3/compactness-anisotropic.
Finiteness of class sets: AA.3/class-number-finite.

For γ∈Γ_{x,U}, Nrd(γ) is a positive rational number that is a unit at every finite place, hence equals 1. Thus Γ lies in the compact real group SL_1(ℍ); as a discrete subgroup it is finite. Apply the finite-adelic-discreteness criterion to the adjoint quotient D^×/ℚ^× for the last claim.
acceptance: For D = (−1, −1)_ℚ and U the units of the Hurwitz order, the class number is 1 and Γ/{±1} has order 12.
For M_2(ℚ) (split, not definite) the quotient is not compact.

sources.match: Exactly the compactness argument.

nodes.title: Volume comparison under level change for a definite quaternion algebra
nodes.statement: For D definite over ℚ and compact open U′ ⊂ U ⊂ (D ⊗ 𝔸_f)^×, with Γ_x = (D^× ∩ xUx⁻¹)/(ℚ^× ∩ U) the finite stabilizers: ∑_{x ∈ Cl(U′)} 1/|Γ′_x| = [U : U′]/[ℚ^× ∩ U : ℚ^× ∩ U′] · ∑_{x ∈ Cl(U)} 1/|Γ_x|, where Cl(U) = D^×\(D ⊗ 𝔸_f)^×/U.
proofSteps: G(ℝ)/ℝ_{>0} is compact. For the effective arithmetic stabilizer modulo its rational central kernel, the quotient volume is this compact-group volume divided by |Γ_x|, with the explicitly chosen full/effective mass convention. ℝ_{>0} is not a subgroup of G(ℝ)^1.
Apply AA.4/level-volume-index (equivalently AA.4/level-map-fibre-mass summed over the base).
acceptance: For the Hurwitz maximal order and an Eichler order of level 3, the local unit index is #ℙ¹(𝔽_3)=4=3+1, so the masses scale by 4 (the rational central intersection is unchanged).

sources.match: The compact-at-infinity case; volumes of the finite class set.

nodes.title: Directed suprema of compatible measures
nodes.statement: Let X be a measurable space, (U_S) a countable directed family of measurable sets covering X and ν_S measures with ν_S supported on U_S and ν_{S'}|_{U_S} = ν_S for S ⊆ S'. Then E ↦ sup_S ν_S(E ∩ U_S) is a measure ν on X with ν|_{U_S} = ν_S for every S, and it is the unique measure with this property.
proofSteps: For a fixed S the map E ↦ ν_{S'}(E ∩ U_{S'}) is monotone in S' and its limit exists in [0, ∞].
Countable additivity: for disjoint E_n, exchange the two monotone suprema sup_S Σ_n = Σ_n sup_S (monotone convergence for series).
Restriction to U_S: for S' ⊇ S, ν_{S'}(E ∩ U_S) = ν_S(E ∩ U_S) by compatibility.
Uniqueness: two measures agreeing on each U_S agree on X = ⋃ U_S by countable additivity over the disjointified pieces.
acceptance: For X = ℝ, U_n = [−n, n] and ν_n Lebesgue measure on U_n, the supremum is Lebesgue measure.

sources.match: The inductive limit of compatible measures.

nodes.title: Normalized local Haar measures
nodes.statement: For a number field K and a finite place v there is a unique additive Haar measure μ_v on K_v with μ_v(𝒪_v) = 1; for a ∈ K_v^×, map (a · ·) μ_v = |a|_v⁻¹ • μ_v with |a|_v = q_v^{−v(a)}.
proofSteps: K_v is a nonarchimedean local field (Tau Ceti), so locally compact with 𝒪_v compact open; normalize Mathlib's Haar measure so that 𝒪_v has volume one.
Scaling: multiplication by a uniformizer maps 𝒪_v onto 𝔪_v, of index q_v in 𝒪_v, so its volume is q_v⁻¹ (MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure); units preserve 𝒪_v.
acceptance: μ_p(pℤ_p) = 1/p for K = ℚ.

sources.match: The normalization. The notes treat additive adele measures; the group-generic argument here is an adaptation, not a quoted general theorem.

nodes.title: Points over a product of rings
nodes.statement: For commutative F-algebras R₁, R₂ (and more generally a finite product), WithConv (H →ₐ[F] R₁ × R₂) ≃* WithConv (H →ₐ[F] R₁) × WithConv (H →ₐ[F] R₂), naturally and as topological groups for the affine-points topology.
hypotheses: H a commutative Hopf algebra over F
proofSteps: An algebra map into a product is a pair of algebra maps (AlgHom.prod); convolution is computed componentwise.
The affine-points topology is induced from R^H, which is the product of R₁^H and R₂^H.
acceptance: G(𝔸_F) = G(F_∞) × G(𝔸_{F,f}) because 𝔸_F = F_∞ × 𝔸_{F,f}.

sources.match: Compatibility with products, here applied to a product of coefficient rings.

nodes.title: Finite adeles as a directed union of S-adeles
nodes.statement: For finite sets S of finite places, the S-adeles 𝔸_{F,S} = ∏_{v∈S} F_v × ∏_{v∉S} 𝒪_v are open subrings of 𝔸_{F,f} forming a directed union, and every F-algebra map H → 𝔸_{F,f} from a finitely generated H restricts to a map of models 𝓗 → 𝔸_{F,S} for S large: G(𝔸_{F,f}) = ⋃_S 𝓗(𝔸_{F,S}).
proofSteps: Each generator of H has finitely many denominators, so its image lies in 𝔸_{F,S} for S large.
Conrad, Theorem 3.4(1) applied to the directed system 𝒪_{F,S} → 𝔸_{F,S} identifies the points over the limit with the limit of the points (Remark 3.5).
acceptance: For G_a: 𝔸_{F,f} = ⋃_S 𝔸_{F,S}.

sources.match: The direct-limit description of adelic points.

nodes.title: The restricted-product bijection on S-adelic points
nodes.statement: For an integral model 𝓗 away from S and S' ⊇ S, the natural map 𝓗(𝔸_{F,S'}) → ∏_{v∈S'} G(F_v) × ∏_{v∉S'} 𝓗(𝒪_v) is a bijection, and a homeomorphism for the affine-points topology on the left and the product topology on the right.
proofSteps: Bijectivity: a map out of the affine 𝓗 into a product ring is a family of maps (points-product-ring for infinite products of rings, the affine case of Conrad Theorem 3.6).
Topology: for affine schemes the affine-points topology commutes with arbitrary products of rings because it is induced from the product topology on coefficient tuples.
acceptance: For GL_n: GL_n(𝔸_{F,S}) = ∏_{v∈S} GL_n(F_v) × ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_v).

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: The modular character on compact and central elements
nodes.statement: For a locally compact group G, the modular character Δ : G → ℝ_{>0} is a continuous homomorphism trivial on every compact subgroup and on the centre of G, and it is invariant under conjugation.
proofSteps: Δ(g) is the scalar by which conjugation by g rescales Haar measure (Mathlib modularCharacter).
A compact subgroup maps to a compact subgroup of ℝ_{>0}, which is trivial.
Conjugation by a central element is the identity.
Δ is a homomorphism to an abelian group, hence constant on conjugacy classes.
acceptance: For the Borel of GL_2(ℚ_p), Δ is trivial on the compact diagonal units diag(ℤ_p^×, ℤ_p^×).

sources.match: Compact quotients do not affect the modular character.

nodes.title: Weyl orbit products lie in the split centre up to finite index
nodes.statement: Let A be a maximal split torus of a connected reductive group over a field and W its relative Weyl group. For a ∈ A(E), the product ∏_{w∈W} w(a) lies in (Z(G) ∩ A)(E) up to an element of a finite group; in particular some power of it lies in the split centre.
proofSteps: The product is W-invariant.
The W-invariants of X_*(A) ⊗ ℚ are X_*(Z ∩ A) ⊗ ℚ (W acts without nonzero fixed vectors on the span of the coroots).
So the W-invariant subtorus is the identity component of Z ∩ A, and A^W is a finite extension of it.
acceptance: For GL_2 and a = diag(x, y): a · w(a) = diag(xy, xy) is central.

sources.match: The unimodularity this lemma serves.

nodes.title: Averaging over a closed subgroup is surjective on compact supports
nodes.statement: For a closed subgroup H of a locally compact group G and a right Haar measure dh on H, the map P : C_c(G) → C_c(H\G), (Pf)(Hg) = ∫_H f(hg) dh, is surjective, and every f ≥ 0 in C_c(H\G) is Pφ for some φ ≥ 0.
hypotheses: dh a right Haar measure on H
proofSteps: Choose a compactly supported continuous ψ ≥ 0 on G with Pψ > 0 on the support of a given F ∈ C_c(H\G) (Bruhat function, via compactness of supports in the quotient).
Put φ = ψ · (F ∘ π)/(Pψ ∘ π); then Pφ = F.
acceptance: For H = {1}, P is the identity of C_c(G).

sources.match: The construction of the invariant measure, of which this surjectivity is the first step.

nodes.title: Weil's functional is well defined under the modular condition
nodes.statement: If Δ_G|_H = Δ_H, then for f ∈ C_c(G), Pf = 0 implies ∫_G f dg = 0; hence Pf ↦ ∫_G f dg is a well-defined positive G-invariant functional on C_c(H\G).
hypotheses: G locally compact Hausdorff; H a closed subgroup
dg and dh right Haar measures
Δ_G|_H = Δ_H, using the pinned Mathlib modular-character convention
proofSteps: Pick φ with Pφ = 1 on the support of f (bruhat-section); then ∫_G f = ∫_G f(g) ∫_H φ(hg) dh dg.

Exchange the integrals and substitute g ↦ h⁻¹g; the modular condition makes the Jacobians cancel, giving ∫_G φ(g) (Pf)(Hg) dg = 0. This calculation requires the right-Haar left-translation and inversion Jacobians, and a support cutoff valid on the projected support; the general argument is a recorded gap.
acceptance: For B ⊂ SL_2(ℝ) the condition fails and the functional is not well defined.

sources.match: The product decomposition that the functional realizes.

nodes.title: Gauge forms under restriction of scalars
nodes.statement: For E/F finite of degree n and a gauge form ω_E on G_E of dimension d, the induced gauge form ω on Res_{E/F} G_E satisfies, at each place v of F, |ω|_v = |d_{E_v/F_v}|_v^{d/2} ∏_{w|v} |ω_E|_w under Res(F_v) ≅ ∏_{w|v} G_E(E_w), where d_{E_v/F_v} is the local discriminant.
proofSteps: Locally Res(F_v) = ∏_{w|v} G_E(E_w), and the top form of a restriction of scalars is the norm of ω_E composed with the determinant of the trace pairing on a basis of E_v over F_v.
The determinant of the trace form in an integral basis is the local discriminant; taking absolute values gives the factor |d|_v^{d/2}.
acceptance: For G_E = G_a and E/F quadratic of discriminant D, the factor is |D|_v^{1/2}.

sources.match: The restriction-of-scalars compatibility these factors serve.

nodes.title: Inductivity of the convergence factors
nodes.statement: For E/F finite and a Galois module X of G_{E} (finite image), the induced module Ind X satisfies L_v(Ind X, s) = ∏_{w|v} L_w(X, s) at every finite place v unramified for X, and the leading coefficients at s = 1 agree.
proofSteps: Mackey: the restriction of Ind X to the decomposition group at v is the sum over w | v of the induced modules from the decomposition groups at w.
Frobenius at w is Frob_v^{f_w}; det(1 − q_v^{-s f_w} Frob_w | X) equals the determinant on the induced block.
acceptance: For X trivial of rank one, ∏_{w|v} (1 − q_w^{-s})⁻¹ is the local factor of ζ_E.

sources.match: The local factors whose induction formula this is.

nodes.title: Reduction for GL_n(ℝ)
nodes.statement: There are C > 0 and a standard Siegel set 𝔖 ⊂ GL_n(ℝ) (with respect to O(n) and the upper triangular Borel) such that GL_n(ℝ) = GL_n(ℤ)·𝔖; equivalently every positive definite form is GL_n(ℤ)-equivalent to an (e, C)-reduced form for the standard basis e.
proofSteps: Hermite–Minkowski reduction: choose successive minima vectors to build a basis in which the Gram matrix is reduced (Siegel's theorem, cited by Borel 3.3).
Translate reducedness into the Siegel-set conditions through reduction-siegel-dictionary.
acceptance: For n = 2 this is the classical reduction of binary forms, giving ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd.

sources.match: The GL_n reduction.

nodes.title: Adelic reduction for GL_n over ℚ
nodes.statement: For a standard Siegel domain 𝔖 of GL_n(ℝ), GL_n(𝔸_ℚ) = GL_n(ℚ) · (𝔖 × GL_n(ℤ̂)).
proofSteps: GL_n(𝔸_f) = GL_n(ℚ)GL_n(ℤ̂) (class number one for GL_n over ℚ, Borel 2.2).
Then reduce the archimedean component by gln-real-reduction, using GL_n(ℚ) ∩ GL_n(ℤ̂) = GL_n(ℤ).

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Reduction for reductive subgroups of GL_n
nodes.statement: Let G ⊂ GL_n be reductive over ℚ with a(G(ℝ))a⁻¹ self-adjoint for some a ∈ SL_n(ℝ). There are finitely many b_i ∈ GL_n(ℚ) such that ⋃_i (a⁻¹𝔖 GL_n(ℤ̂) b_i ∩ G(𝔸)) is a fundamental set for G(ℚ) in G(𝔸).
proofSteps: Realize G as the stabilizer of a point w with closed GL_n-orbit in a rational representation (Borel–Harish-Chandra 3.8).
Finiteness: the points of w·GL_n(𝔸_ℚ)(𝔖 GL_n(ℤ̂)) meeting w·GL_n(ℚ) are finite in number (Borel 3.4, 4.3).
Combine with gln-adelic-covering.
acceptance: For G = SL_n the single b = 1 suffices.

sources.match: Exactly the setting.

nodes.title: Rational points on closed orbits
nodes.statement: Let G be reductive over F, H ⊂ G a reductive F-subgroup and σ : G → H\G. Then σ_𝔸(G(𝔸)) ∩ (H\G)(F) is a finite union of G(F)-orbits.
proofSteps: H\G is affine (Matsushima), realized as a closed orbit w·ρ(G) in a rational representation (Borel 5.3).
For a fundamental set Ω with property (F3), w·ρ_𝔸(Ω) ∩ F^n is finite (Borel 4.6), which gives finitely many orbits (Borel 5.4).
acceptance: For G = GL_n acting on quadratic forms, the forms in a genus form finitely many classes.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Siegel sets in G(𝔸)^1 have finite measure
nodes.statement: For an adelic Siegel set 𝔖 = 𝔖(T₁, ω), the measure of 𝔖 ∩ G(𝔸)^1 is finite.
proofSteps: By the Iwasawa integration formula, the measure of 𝔖 ∩ G(𝔸)^1 is at most vol(ω) vol(K) ∫ e^{−2ρ_0(H_0(a))} da over {a ∈ A_0(ℝ)^0 ∩ G(𝔸)^1 : β(H_0(a) − T₁) > 0}.
On the cone shifted by T₁, 2ρ_0 is a positive combination of the simple roots, so the integral of the exponential converges (a product of one-dimensional integrals of e^{−c t} over t > t₀).
acceptance: For SL_2/ℚ, the classical Siegel set {|x| ≤ 1/2, y > t} has hyperbolic area ∫∫ dx dy/y² < ∞.

sources.match: Siegel sets modulo the centre and their volumes.

nodes.title: Finitely many G(𝒪)-orbits on rational flags
nodes.statement: For connected G and an F-parabolic P, (G/P)(F) is a finite union of orbits of an arithmetic subgroup; equivalently G(F) = ⋃_{i∈I} Γ x_i P(F) with I finite.
proofSteps: G/P is projective, so (G/P)(𝔸) is compact and G(𝔸) = C·P(𝔸) for a compact C (Godement, Borel 7.2).
Cover C by finitely many translates of an open compact subgroup and use class-number-finite for P.
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ) acting on ℙ¹(ℚ) there is one orbit (one cusp).

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Strong approximation through finitely many places
nodes.statement: For S containing the archimedean places, G has strong approximation with respect to S iff for every finite set S₁ of places disjoint from S, the S ∪ S₁-arithmetic group G(𝒪(S ∪ S₁)) is dense in G_{S₁} = ∏_{v∈S₁} G(F_v).
proofSteps: Basic open sets of G(𝔸^S) are products of opens at finitely many places S₁ and integral points elsewhere (AA.1/compact-open-product).
Density of G(F) in such a set is density of the elements integral outside S ∪ S₁ in the open of G_{S₁}.
acceptance: For SL_2/ℚ and S = {∞}: density of SL_2(ℤ[1/p]) in SL_2(ℚ_p) for every p.

sources.match: Exactly the reformulation.

nodes.title: S-arithmetic groups are not discrete at an extra place
nodes.statement: If G is absolutely almost simple, G_S is noncompact and S₁ is finite, nonempty and disjoint from S, then the image of G(𝒪(S ∪ S₁)) in G_{S₁} is not discrete and is infinite.
hypotheses: F a number field; G connected absolutely almost simple
S finite containing the archimedean places
S₁ finite, nonempty and disjoint from S
proofSteps: G(𝒪(S ∪ S₁)) is a lattice in G_{S∪S₁} (AA.3/s-arithmetic-lattice) while G(𝒪(S)) is a lattice in G_S.

If its image in G_{S₁} were discrete, G(𝒪(S ∪ S₁)) ∩ (G_S × open compact) would be a lattice in G_S of covolume tending to infinity as the compact shrinks, contradicting finiteness of covolume (Platonov–Rapinchuk Lemma 3.17).
acceptance: SL_2(ℤ[1/p]) is dense, not discrete, in SL_2(ℚ_p).

sources.match: Exactly the step.

nodes.title: Principal units of small radius are torsion free
nodes.statement: In an algebraic closure of ℚ_p, the multiplicative group {λ : |λ − 1|_p < p^{−1/(p−1)}} contains no root of unity other than 1; in particular eigenvalues of elements of 1 + pM_n(ℤ_p) (p ≥ 3) or 1 + 4M_n(ℤ_2) generate a torsion-free group.
proofSteps: A primitive ℓ-th root of unity ζ with ℓ prime to p has |ζ − 1|_p = 1.
A primitive p^k-th root of unity has |ζ − 1|_p = p^{−1/(p^{k−1}(p−1))} ≥ p^{−1/(p−1)}.
The set is a group (ultrametric inequality), and eigenvalues of a matrix in 1 + pM_n(ℤ_p) satisfy |λ − 1|_p ≤ p⁻¹ < p^{−1/(p−1)} for p ≥ 3.
acceptance: −1 ∈ 1 + 2ℤ_2 but −1 ∉ 1 + 4ℤ_2: the level 4 is needed at p = 2.

sources.match: The neatness criterion, whose p-adic input this lemma is.

nodes.title: Free action of finite level groups at neat level
nodes.statement: For neat compact open U, normal open U′⊂U, and K∞ containing A_G(ℝ)^0 and compact modulo it, the full group U/U′ acts freely and properly discontinuously on X_{U′}. Rational stabilizers are finite, and neatness makes them trivial; the central rational kernel is trivial in this scope.
hypotheses: K∞ contains A_G(ℝ)^0 and is compact modulo it
proofSteps: The stabilizer of [g] is the image of G(F) ∩ g K_∞U g⁻¹, a finite group (discrete ∩ compact modulo the split centre).
The actual stabilizer is finite and torsion free by neatness, so it is {1}. In particular its central subgroup is also trivial.
Proper discontinuity because U/U′ is finite.
acceptance: For GL_2/ℚ at U(3), U/U(9) acts freely on Y(9).

sources.match: Free quotients at small level.

nodes.title: GL_2(ℝ) modulo ℝ^× SO(2)
nodes.statement: GL_2(ℝ)/ℝ^× SO(2) is homeomorphic to ℍ^± = ℂ ∖ ℝ through g ↦ g·i, equivariantly for the Möbius action; GL_2(ℝ)^+ acts transitively on ℍ with stabilizer ℝ^× SO(2) at i.
proofSteps: Use upper-half-plane-action-conventions for the raw action on ℍ±. For x+iy with y>0, the matrix (sqrt(y), x/sqrt(y); 0, 1/sqrt(y)) sends i there. Negative determinant reaches the lower half-plane; the stabilizer of i is ℝ^×SO(2).
The stabilizer of i in GL_2(ℝ)^+ is ℝ_{>0}·SO(2) up to ±1; complex conjugation exchanges ℍ and its conjugate.
acceptance: diag(1, −1) maps i to −i.

sources.match: Transitivity of G(ℝ) on X = ℍ^±.

nodes.title: Pushforward of a homogeneous measure to a compact abelian quotient
nodes.statement: Let C be a compact abelian group, π : G → C a continuous surjective homomorphism, T ≤ G a closed subgroup with Λ ≤ T discrete and Λ\T compact (as for [T(𝔸)] with T anisotropic modulo the centre), and μ the T-invariant probability measure on Λ\T g. If π(Λ) = 1, then π_*μ is the Haar probability measure of the coset π(T)·π(g) of the closed subgroup π(T).
proofSteps: π_*μ is invariant under π(T).
A probability measure on a coset invariant under the subgroup is its Haar measure (uniqueness of Haar measure on the compact group π(T)).
π(T) is closed: it is the image of the compact Λ\T under the continuous map induced by π.
acceptance: For T = G, π_*μ is the Haar probability measure of C.

sources.locator: Definition 3.1, arXiv v3 p. 22; Annals p. 169
sources.match: The pushforward principle, here for homogeneous toral measures.

nodes.title: Kernels of distinct characters converge to the whole group
nodes.statement: Let C be a compact abelian group and (χ_i) a sequence of pairwise distinct continuous characters C → {±1}. Then the closed subgroups ker χ_i converge to C in the Chabauty topology; consequently any weak-* limit of probability measures invariant under ker χ_i is C-invariant.
proofSteps: The Pontryagin dual of C is discrete, so a sequence of distinct characters leaves every finite set.
Chabauty–Pontryagin duality: the annihilators ⟨χ_i⟩ converge to the trivial subgroup, hence ker χ_i converges to C.
Invariance passes to weak-* limits along Chabauty-convergent subgroups.
acceptance: For C = ℚ^×\𝔸^×/𝔸^{×2}, distinct quadratic characters χ_{E_i} have kernels converging to C.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.6, arXiv v3 p. 25; Annals pp. 172–173
sources.match: Exactly the argument.

nodes.title: Borel fundamental domains for countable discrete subgroups
nodes.statement: Let G be a second countable locally compact Hausdorff group and Γ ≤ G a countable discrete subgroup acting by left translation. There is a Borel set D ⊂ G meeting every orbit Γg in exactly one point.
hypotheses: G second countable locally compact Hausdorff
proofSteps: Choose an open neighbourhood V of 1 with VV⁻¹ ∩ Γ = {1}. Each right translate Vg injects into Γ\G: γv₁g=v₂g implies γ=v₂v₁⁻¹=1.

Cover G by countably many right translates Vg_n and define D = union over n of (Vg_n minus union over m<n of ΓVg_m). The Γ-saturations are Borel because Γ is countable. Every orbit is retained exactly once in its first such translate.
acceptance: For ℤ ⊂ ℝ, the construction yields a Borel set such as [0, 1).

sources.match: Fundamental sets; here exact fundamental domains.

nodes.title: Corrected volumes for GL_n and SL_n
nodes.statement: For the standard models of GL_n and SL_n over 𝒪_F and their standard gauge forms, at every finite place v: λ_v · #GL_n(k_v) q_v^{-n²} = ∏_{i=2}^{n} (1 − q_v^{-i}) with λ_v = (1 − q_v^{-1})^{-1}, and #SL_n(k_v) q_v^{-(n²−1)} = ∏_{i=2}^{n} (1 − q_v^{-i}); both products over v converge absolutely.
proofSteps: Apply weil-volume-formula; Σ_v q_v^{-2} converges because Σ_v q_v^{-s} converges for s > 1 (Dedekind zeta).

sources.match: The convergence, here checked by counting for GL_n and SL_n.

nodes.title: Arithmetic quotients have finite volume
nodes.statement: For connected reductive G over F and Γ = G(F) ∩ U with U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) compact open, Γ\(G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0) has finite invariant volume.
proofSteps: By component-decomposition, Γ\(G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0) is one of finitely many pieces of G(F)\G(𝔸)/A_G(ℝ)^0 U, which is the quotient of G(F)\G(𝔸)^1 by the compact U.
finite-volume gives the finiteness.
acceptance: SL_2(ℤ)\SL_2(ℝ) has finite volume.

sources.match: Passage between the adelic and the arithmetic quotient.

nodes.title: Division algebras have no nontrivial unipotent units
nodes.statement: If D is a division algebra over a field of characteristic 0, then D^× contains no unipotent element other than 1.
proofSteps: If u is unipotent then (u − 1)^m = 0 for some m; in a division algebra this forces u − 1 = 0.
acceptance: In Hamilton's quaternions over ℚ every unit other than 1 has a non-nilpotent u − 1.

sources.match: Exactly the argument.

nodes.title: Arithmetic quotients of anisotropic groups are compact
nodes.statement: In the setting of arithmetic-quotient-finite-volume, Γ\(G(F_∞)/A_G(ℝ)^0) is compact iff G^der is F-anisotropic; for an anisotropic inner form SL_1(D) of a central division algebra D, H(F)\H(𝔸_F) and Γ\H(F_∞) are compact.
proofSteps: Same reduction as arithmetic-quotient-finite-volume, now with compactness-anisotropic and compactness-isotropic.
SL_1(D) for a division algebra D has no nontrivial unipotent rational points (division-algebra-no-unipotent: a unipotent u ≠ 1 gives the nilpotent u − 1 ≠ 0 in D).
acceptance: For D definite quaternion over ℚ, Γ is finite modulo the centre and Γ\D^×(ℝ)/ℝ_{>0} is compact.

sources.match: The compactness criterion transported to arithmetic quotients.

nodes.title: Level quotients are Hausdorff
nodes.statement: For compact open U and K_∞ compact modulo A_G(ℝ)^0 containing A_G(ℝ)^0, the level quotient X_U is Hausdorff and locally compact, and G(F) acts properly discontinuously on G(𝔸)/K_∞U.
proofSteps: G(F) is discrete in G(𝔸) (AA.1/rational-points-discrete) and K_∞U is compact modulo the central A_G(ℝ)^0, so for compact sets C, C′ only finitely many γ satisfy γC ∩ C′K_∞U ≠ ∅.
A quotient of a locally compact Hausdorff space by a properly discontinuous group action is Hausdorff and locally compact.
acceptance: SL_2(ℤ)\ℍ is Hausdorff.

sources.match: The topology of level quotients.

nodes.title: Degree of a Hecke correspondence
nodes.statement: For compact open U and g ∈ G(𝔸_f), the double coset UgU is the disjoint union of [U : U ∩ gUg⁻¹] left cosets of U, and at neat level p₁ : X_{U ∩ gUg⁻¹} → X_U has degree [U : U ∩ gUg⁻¹] modulo the central correction.
proofSteps: UgU/U ≅ U/(U ∩ gUg⁻¹) (orbit–stabilizer for U acting on G/U); Tau Ceti HeckeCoset.degree_eq_relIndex states this for abstract Hecke cosets.
Combine with level-covering-map for the inclusion U ∩ gUg⁻¹ ⊂ U.
acceptance: For GL_2/ℚ, U = GL_2(ℤ̂), g = diag(p,1): p + 1.

sources.match: Hecke operators from double cosets, whose degree this lemma computes.

nodes.title: Units at level U_Q form a lattice of rank r₁ + r₂ − 1
nodes.statement: For a compact open U ⊂ Ô^×, Γ_U = F^× ∩ U is a finite-index subgroup of 𝒪_F^×, and its image under the logarithmic embedding is a lattice of rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 in the trace-zero hyperplane of ℝ^{r₁+r₂}.
proofSteps: F^× ∩ Ô^× = 𝒪_F^×, and U has finite index in Ô^×, so Γ_U has finite index in 𝒪_F^×.
Dirichlet's unit theorem (Mathlib: the unit lattice has rank Units.rank F); a finite-index subgroup of a lattice is a lattice of the same rank.
acceptance: For F = ℚ(√2), Γ is generated up to torsion by a power of 1 + √2.

sources.match: The unit lattice whose quotient gives the torus components.

nodes.title: Topology of the infinite-adele mixed-space comparison
nodes.statement: The canonical ring equivalence ringEquiv_mixedSpace F and its inverse are continuous for the product topologies, so it upgrades to a ring homeomorphism.
proofSteps: Split the finite place-index set into real and complex subtypes. Use the pinned real and complex completion isometry equivalences coordinatewise, and reindex the products. Their homeomorphisms and the finite product homeomorphism have exactly the underlying ringEquiv_mixedSpace maps.
acceptance: For ℚ the map is the real completion identification; for ℚ(i) it is the complex completion identification.

sources.match: Supplies the archimedean product carrier. Continuity in this packet is deduced from the pinned local isometry equivalences, rather than attributed to this passage.

nodes.title: Inversion between left and right quotient conventions
nodes.statement: For a locally compact unimodular G and discrete countable Γ, inversion sends Γg to g⁻¹Γ, giving a homeomorphism Γ\G≃G/Γ that preserves the correspondingly normalized quotient measures. It carries left-orbit unfolding to the pinned right Γ.op-orbit unfolding.
hypotheses: G second countable locally compact Hausdorff and unimodular
Γ a countable discrete subgroup; normalized Haar μ is left and right invariant
Use the fundamental-domain quotient measures and the integrability/measurability hypotheses of the pinned theorem
proofSteps: If g′=γg then (g′)⁻¹=g⁻¹γ⁻¹, so inversion descends; its inverse is inversion. Quotient continuity follows from continuity of inversion.

Inversion preserves a bi-invariant Haar measure; it exchanges left and right fundamental domains. Transport the quotient pushforwards and the integrable automorphization formula, retaining its AEStronglyMeasurable hypothesis.
acceptance: For ℤ⊂ℝ the bridge is x mod ℤ↦−x mod ℤ and preserves circle volume.

sources.match: The left-orbit convention used by Arthur; the bridge is an elementary derivation from inversion and the pinned right-orbit theorem.

nodes.title: Raw Möbius action and the Mathlib folded action
nodes.statement: The raw Möbius maps of GL₂(ℝ) induce an action on ℍ±=ℂ∖ℝ. Folding the lower half-plane by conjugation is equivariant for this action and Mathlib glAction on ℍ. For positive determinant the raw and folded formulas coincide; diag(1,−1) sends i to −i in the raw action and fixes i in glAction. The existing pinned imaginary-part and denominator formulas supply the carrier and sign checks.
proofSteps: Use the pinned moebius_im and denom_ne_zero_of_im formulas to preserve ℂ∖ℝ. Direct matrix multiplication and the nonzero denominators prove the action law. The raw maps commute with complex conjugation because their coefficients are real.

Folding z to z or its conjugate according to its imaginary sign is equivariant: positive determinant preserves both half-planes and negative determinant swaps them. Compare with coe_smul and its σ definition. The source quotient uses this raw action; no new scalar-formula declaration is planned.
acceptance: diag(1,−1) distinguishes the two actions at i.

sources.match: The full real-orbit convention; the explicit folding bridge is derived by matrix algebra.

Transport the corrected raw/folded GL₂ real action and both O(2)/SO(2) component conventions through the canonical topology and level choices.

Verify GL₁ quotient/cohomology/Hecke tests for the specified level and archimedean torus; resolve full/effective quaternion mass normalization. The explicit Hurwitz/Eichler class-number input remains open.

gaps.title: Measures of gauge forms on nonarchimedean analytic groups
gaps.detail: Defining |ω|_v on G(F_v) for a nonarchimedean local field F_v needs the F_v-analytic manifold structure of G(F_v) for smooth G and the change-of-variables formula μ(ψ(U)) = ∫_U |det Dψ|_v dμ for F_v-analytic diffeomorphisms ψ between open subsets of F_v^d. Mathlib has the inverse function theorem over complete normed fields and the real change-of-variables theorem, but not its p-adic analogue, and no layer of the atlas plans it (searched: 'analytic manifold', 'p-adic Lie', 'change of variables'). The archimedean case is covered by Mathlib's real change of variables.

gaps.title: Leading coefficient of Artin L-functions at s = 1
gaps.detail: For a connected group G whose character module X*(G_{F̄}) has nontrivial Galois action, the constant ρ_G needs the meromorphic continuation of the Artin L-function L(X, s) to a neighbourhood of s = 1 and the nonvanishing at s = 1 of L(σ, s) for the nontrivial irreducible constituents σ (Brauer induction and the nonvanishing of Hecke L-functions at s = 1). No layer of the atlas plans Artin L-functions of number fields in this generality (atlas search 'Artin L' finds only function-field and Iwasawa layers), and the libraries lack them. The split case (trivial Galois action), which covers GL_n, split tori and every semisimple group, uses only the residue of the Dedekind zeta function (Mathlib).

gaps.title: Orders of finite reductive groups (Steinberg's formula)
gaps.detail: Absolute convergence of the Tamagawa product needs #𝓗(k_v) = q_v^d ∏_i (1 - ε_i q_v^{-d_i}) for connected reductive groups over finite fields, or at least #𝓗(k_v) q_v^{-d} = L_v(X, 1)^{-1}(1 + O(q_v^{-2})) uniformly in v (Lang's theorem and the Bruhat decomposition over 𝔽_q). Neither library has it and no atlas layer plans it (searched 'Steinberg', '#G(F_q)', 'Lang's theorem'). The cases GL_n and SL_n are elementary counts.

gaps.title: Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem for p-adic analytic groups
gaps.detail: The openness of the p-adic closure of a Zariski-dense subgroup (Rapinchuk Lemma 2.7) uses Cartan's theorem that a closed subgroup of a p-adic analytic group is an analytic subgroup with a Lie algebra, together with the irreducibility of the adjoint representation of an absolutely almost simple group. Neither library has p-adic analytic groups and no atlas layer plans this theorem (searched 'Cartan', 'p-adic Lie', 'analytic group').

gaps.title: Borel density theorem
gaps.detail: Zariski density of infinite S-arithmetic subgroups of absolutely almost simple groups with G_S noncompact (Platonov–Rapinchuk Theorem 4.10, cited by Rapinchuk §2.4) is planned in no layer and absent from the libraries; Platonov–Rapinchuk is not freely available and the proof (Furstenberg's projective-measure argument) is not read here.

gaps.title: Kneser's and Harder–Chernousov's Galois-cohomology theorems
gaps.detail: Kneser's vanishing of H¹(F_v, G) for simply connected semisimple G at nonarchimedean v, the Hasse principle of Kneser–Harder–Chernousov and weak approximation for simply connected groups (Platonov–Rapinchuk Theorems 6.4, 6.6, 7.8, cited by Harpaz–Wittenberg §6) are stated here with their exact hypotheses, but their proofs (classification-based, using Bruhat–Tits theory and case-by-case work for E8) are not decomposed: the book is not freely available and no atlas layer plans the classification of simply connected groups over local and global fields.

gaps.title: Nonnormal Weil quotient integration with right Haar measures
gaps.detail: Construct the compact-support averaging lift for an arbitrary closed H, justify compactness and continuity on H\G, prove the right-Haar modular Jacobian calculation and positivity, and obtain the quotient Radon measure by Riesz. The pinned IsSES.inducedMeasure constructs a measure on the middle group of a normal extension from already supplied Haar measures on subgroup and quotient; it is not this theorem. Arthur §1 states the discrete/unimodular cases, not the full proof. Split the cutoff, functional and extension-to-integrable-functions arguments into lemma nodes with exact analytic prerequisites.

gaps.title: Convergent infinite rescaling and number-field Tamagawa normalization
gaps.detail: Prove the box formula and model/exceptional-set independence for a product of positive local volumes with summable logarithms, by normalizing every good factor and multiplying by the convergent total product. Supply a public number-field source for |d_F|^(−dim G/2), the chosen real/complex base measures, and the Artin leading coefficient. Rosengarten §3 is explicitly function-field-only and cannot be converted merely by replacing q^(1−g) by a discriminant: its logarithm/cokernel factors have no such literal replacement. The suggested measure_eq_product uses arbitrary ρ, λ_v and μ∞ ; finprod has been replaced by tprod, but convergence and canonical factor hypotheses still need to be expressed; it is not the canonical theorem.

gaps.title: Central-character Hilbert bundles, character extension and Fourier decomposition
gaps.detail: Prove closedness of 𝔛G(F), measurable-section/cocycle or associated-line-bundle construction, Hilbert completeness and strong continuity. For 𝔛′⊂𝔛, extend the compatible character ω′ to ω₀ on 𝔛Z(F), then twist right translation by ω₀⁻¹ to obtain an action of the compact quotient C. Untwisted translation does not descend to C when ω′ is nontrivial. Supply Pontryagin character extension and compact abelian Peter–Weyl with quotient-measure normalization.

gaps.title: Proper algebraic adelic heights and polynomial rational-point counting
gaps.detail: Split properness, polynomial inverse control, finite-place polynomial comparison and rational-point counting into lemma nodes. Counting requires a quantitative lattice/denominator estimate, not merely discreteness and compact height balls. Arthur §13 is written over ℚ; justify the number-field transport and complex multiplicities. Corrected Hilbert–Schmidt height has identity m^([F:ℚ]/2), not 1. The suggested abstract point-group representations do not provide algebraic matrix coefficients or the required properness.

gaps.title: Independent reduction inputs and removal of mathematical proof cycles
gaps.detail: The literal prerequisite graph is acyclic, but proof text uses class-number-finite to obtain adelic Siegel covering while class-number-finite uses that covering; self-adjoint reduction cites closed-orbit finiteness whose proof invokes fundamental-set reduction; real finite-overlap and adelic finite-overlap invoke each other. Follow Borel §4.3–4.5: establish arithmetic GL_n lattice reduction, closed-orbit realization and the required lattice-intersection finiteness independently (the facts in §3 and §4.3), then self-adjoint reduction and class-number finiteness. Borel 5.4 is a later consequence, not that primitive input. Name each direct nonroutine fact and dismantle these cycles before marking the stage planned.

gaps.title: Parabolic Iwasawa Jacobian and quasi-invariant integration
gaps.detail: For a proper parabolic P of a reductive G, Δ_G|P=1 and Δ_P generally differs from 1. The invariant-measure construction on P\G cannot be used. Prove the N-M-K or P-K integration/Jacobian formula with δ_P⁻¹ and the compact intersection quotient, using quasi-invariant integration rather than an invariant measure on P\G. Separate existence of local/global Iwasawa factorization from the integration formula and convergence of the root integral.

gaps.title: Fixed-K Siegel containment, rational orbit preimages and reduced-form dictionary
gaps.detail: The BKT erratum gives corrected statements and cites the nonroutine proofs. Read/decompose the corrected rational preimage theorem [BGST23, Theorem 28.1, published Proposition 3.4], the Cartan-stable containment argument and the explicit incompatible-map example. Borel–Harish-Chandra 7.5 only concerns a real Siegel set and is not the rational finite-translate statement (source issue E9). Supply the positive-form/GL versus determinant-one symmetric-space normalization in the reduced-form dictionary. HoroData in the prototype omits the Levi, Cartan and root-basis axioms, so an arbitrary decomposition cannot supply these claims.

gaps.title: Arithmetic native-field and several-place strong approximation
gaps.detail: Rapinchuk §2.6 proves the Lie-algebra openness step over ℚ with one extra isotropic prime; general number-field and several-place/anisotropic cases are referred to Platonov–Rapinchuk §7.4, not proved there. Supply the arithmetic restriction-of-scalars/Lie-algebra argument that excludes subfield subgroups, the extra-place nondiscreteness lemma, and the finite-product closure argument with its actual factor decomposition. Corrected ℚ_p openness cannot be applied to arbitrary F_v. S₁ is finite, disjoint from S and nonempty for the nondiscreteness statement; anisotropic local groups are not covered by the Kneser–Tits finite-index consequence.

gaps.title: Algebraic neatness, stable lattices and root-of-unity valuations
gaps.detail: Decompose the algebraic representation-independence argument (weights/subquotients of tensor powers of a faithful algebraic representation), existence of a stable integral lattice for compact matrix groups, and the p-adic valuation bound for nontrivial roots of unity used by the one-prime criterion. Abstract faithful homomorphisms of point groups, as in the suggested file, are not algebraic representations and do not supply independence. No exact supplier declaration is listed for these nonroutine facts. REV-FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1~3 repairs the neatness representation-independence and existence signatures to require actual GL_n coordinate morphisms, surjective for the chosen faithful representation, through the pinned Tau Ceti carrier. This removes the arbitrary-point-homomorphism overstatement in those signatures. The tensor/weight proof, stable lattice construction and p-adic root-of-unity estimates remain distinct requested inputs; no completion of their Lean proofs or of the broader packet is claimed.

gaps.title: Compact-modulo-split-centre stabilizers and effective versus full masses
gaps.detail: Supply the lemma that rational stabilizers with compact finite level have archimedean H_G=0 and hence meet K∞ in a compact subgroup when K∞/A_G is compact. Construct quotient topologies and proper actions before invoking covering theorems. Distinguish full groupoid automorphisms from effective stabilizers modulo the rational centre in the mass formula: the existing SL₂ elliptic example has full order 4 and effective order 2. For general Shimura K∞ with a larger noncompact centre, unit stabilizers may be infinite; the compact-modulo-A_G theorem cannot silently be used there. The prototype only assumes compact K∞ and arbitrary topology instances, ; the neat test now includes compactness of U and concludes triviality, but the canonical quotient topology and larger compact-modulo-A_G scope remain to be expressed. Normality identifies the canonical principal U/U′ action; it does not identify the full deck-transformation group of a disconnected cover. For G_m/ℚ, K∞=ℝ^× and principal levels 3 and 15, the base is one point and the fibre has four points, with full deck group S₄ but canonical level group (ℤ/5)^×=C₄.

gaps.title: Almost-everywhere integral lifting of abelianization
gaps.detail: A pointwise local H¹-vanishing theorem does not supply a lift in the restricted product. For the reductive simply connected derived group, prove smooth integral models and integral lifts at almost every good finite place, using connected fibres and Lang over the residue field, then Hensel lifting. Identify the actual derived simply connected cover, not an arbitrary Hopf map. The suggested plus-subgroup and residual quotient tests use arbitrary covers/equivalences; the PGL₂ residual test now uses a square-class-valued determinant and includes surjectivity and the principal-diagonal compatibility, but these must be supplied by the actual algebraic determinant.

gaps.title: Residual compactness, character kernels and homogeneous-measure limits
gaps.detail: Prove residual compactness independently of the component theorem that consumes it, using the correct idele square-class quotient and finite image at almost all unit factors. Supply compact abelian duality/Chabauty or Fourier convergence of distinct character kernels, and justify pushforward of homogeneous Haar measure to its image, including characterwise limits. These are nonroutine harmonic-analysis inputs missing from the direct prerequisite lists. The local quotient G(𝔸)/G(𝔸)^+ itself is not compact (source issue E6).

gaps.title: Basis-sensitive gauge-form restriction and discriminant normalization
gaps.detail: Specify a basis/determinant-line construction of the F-gauge form induced from an E-form, then compute its local measure and global discriminant factor. The cited Rosengarten introduction states desired compatibility but no local discriminant formula. For E=ℚ(√5), v=5 and G_a with integral-basis coordinate form dx₁∧dx₂, both coordinate Haar and the E-local Haar give the integer ring mass 1, while the asserted |disc|_v^(1/2) is 5^(−1/2). Thus the displayed formula is false for that natural interpretation and underdetermined without a convention. Replace it with a proved basis-sensitive theorem, decompose Artin induction, then derive the global restriction identity.

gaps.title: Finite-type and supplier-faithful suggested declarations
gaps.detail: Repair the suggested signatures against the packet and the pinned imports: affine groups must be finite type with the required connected/reductive/geometrically reduced properties; IntegralModel needs finite presentation and a Hopf-compatible generic fibre; WeilRestrictionPoints needs naturality and its morphism/tower commuting squares; parabolics and admissible compacts need their actual structural predicates; torsors need coaction and equivariance axioms; weak/strong approximation needs the declared place sets; simply connectedness needs central isogenies onto a semisimple group, not every surjective Hopf map; neatness needs algebraic representations; level translations need archimedean component 1 (or normalization of K∞). Correct the component quotient to divide by the finite-supported image of U, not the comap under finite projection. Use the real raw/folded action bridge. The compiled Mathlib-only stand-ins do not validate these mathematical signatures, and several tests assert equivalent carriers supplied as hypotheses rather than checking canonical examples.
